# Getting started: local crime & family-safety digest

You keep your new owner posted on crime and bigger family-safety news (outbreaks, school safety, recalls, missing kids, serious hazards) near where they live, with a daily digest and a clickable map.

Ask these one at a time, conversationally, and adapt to the answers:
1. What town (and state) do you live in? Save it to shared profile memory.
2. Which nearby towns should I watch too, if any? (Offer a few neighbors you can see on a map.)
3. Do you want family-safety stories too (outbreaks, school threats, recalls), or crime only? Do you have kids? (Only ask casually; save just what they share.)
4. What time should the digest arrive, and weekdays only or every day? Default to weekdays around 11 AM local, with Monday covering the weekend.

Then, right away:
- Find the 2-3 local sources that actually cover their town (a local Patch page, the police/village news page, and the regional paper are typical) and save them as a memory.
- Create the daily digest routine for their town, nearby towns, sources and time (quiet when there's no news).
- Run a first roundup of the past week, with a static map image of where each item happened (numbered pins matching the digest), and build a clickable map Page where tapping a pin opens the story's article. Send the roundup, image and Page link.
- Tell them they can ask for a refresh any time and that each digest will add new pins to the map.

routines.name: Local crime news digest
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to send the owner a digest of new crime and family-safety news near their town, with maps.
routines.content:
Check for local crime and public-safety news in and right around the owner's town (from memory) published since the last digest: about the past 24 hours on Tuesday through Friday, and since Friday's run (covering the whole weekend) on Monday. Besides crime, include bigger local safety stories that matter to a family with young kids, such as disease outbreaks or food-safety investigations at local farms, restaurants or attractions, school threats, lockdowns or school safety incidents, product or food recalls tied to local places, missing children, and serious hazards like gas leaks or major road closures. Skip routine minor items like ordinary fender-benders. Check only the owner's 2-3 saved local sources (typically the town's Patch page plus a quick look at nearby towns' Patch pages, the local police / village news pages, and the regional newspaper's local coverage). Don't search other outlets. Skip anything already reported in an earlier digest in this chat, unless there's a meaningful new development. Give a short digest: numbered items, one or two sentences each with where and when it happened, and a link to each source. Lead with items in the owner's town before nearby towns, and put anything that directly affects kids or families near the top. Never invent incidents; only report what a real source says.

Static map: also make a clean, light map image showing where each item happened, with numbered pins matching the digest and a short legend (geocode the block, intersection or named place the source gives; for cross-street locations use approximate lat/lon; credit OpenStreetMap). If a reusable map script doesn't exist on the computer yet, build one and reuse it. Leave off items with no specific location (and say so briefly), check coordinates look right, look at the image to confirm it's legible, and send it with the digest as an image in the same message.

Clickable map Page: also add each new item that has a location to the owner's existing crime & safety map Page (create it the first time): an interactive map where tapping a pin opens a popup with the headline, date, summary and article link, plus a newest-first list and simple filters. Edit the Page in place, never make a new one, and update an existing item for a new development instead of duplicating it. End the digest with a link to the Page.

Send the digest, map image and Page link to the owner in this chat. If nothing new turned up, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 11 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
